short: Standard training recipe (M03) at larger scale: pretrain on 26, calibrate 3 min. The closed corpus carries the result: unseen sentences give 99.9% WER (M12, behind).
position: The paper [@le2026multisubject] changes training (M03): pretraining on the other members of a 27-person cohort, then calibrating on the held-out one. The design is standard: sEMG decoders have been pretrained on other speakers and adapted to a new one since 2008 [@wand2008speakeradaptive; @wu2022picnn; @scheck2024crossspeaker]; cohort size and a 1-to-26 pool sweep combined with minute-level calibration budgets are what it adds. The strongest confound is the closed corpus: other participants' repetitions of the five test sentences stay in pretraining (§3.2), and once those sentences leave all training, CER rises from 21.7% to 78.6% and WER from 31.9% to 99.9% (Table 3). The 3-minute result thus measures how fast a model recognizes sentences already seen from other people. The evaluation (M12) is behind the best comparable work, which reports silent-EMG error on sentences absent from training [@gaddy2021improved; @benster2024monalisa].
